junction.name: Market Street & Gough Street, San Francisco

claims.text: Market Street & Gough Street had 29 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
These counts are Market Street & Gough Street's own: the city's record places 32 of the 61 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $2.0 million a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's worst crash locations.

This corner got continental crosswalks. Across the city: at 780 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (+4%, 95% interval -25% to +33%) could be zero. The city's own record neither shows it worked nor rules it out, so repeating it here rests on other evidence.
The city's painted safety zones: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (+2%, 95% interval -20% to +34%) could be zero); a second run of the same design on 780 sites agrees.
Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 0.9 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $298,000 a year.
Leading Pedestrian Interval would avoid about 0.1 crashes a year (CMF 9918, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $18,000 a year.

The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) is responsible for Gough Street, Haight Street, Market Street, Rose Street, Stevenson Street, Valencia Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) is ready to draft from these facts.

agent.summary: Market Street & Gough Street ranks #2 in San Francisco with 61 injury crashes since 2021-10-31. Crashes have no over-represented pattern vs city worst locations, but include 15 vehicle-bicycle and 6 pedestrian events. The corner already has continental crosswalks, which the city's record has not shown to reduce pedestrian injury crashes, so repeating visibility enhancements is not supported. Effective low-cost signal fixes (yellow interval increase and retroreflective backplates) are estimated to avoid ~3.3 and 1.8 injury crashes per year. Ownership is SFMTA.
